topic: kafka:Consumer lag: Latency vs Throughput trade-off
text:
We often assume lag is a resource problem, but it is a policy failure.

Most candidates walk through the standard JVM thread pool tuning. They discuss ThreadPoolExecutor configurations, core count adjustments, or the transition to virtual threads to maximize throughput.

It sounds correct until you have lived it. Strong resumes usually stop here, focusing on the mechanics of processing faster rather than the physics of the queue.

Nothing timed out. Everything was late.

I let them keep talking about maximizing worker efficiency. I almost interrupted when they suggested increasing the internal buffer size to absorb traffic spikes.

I waited for them to mention the producer. They focused on the latency of the individual task, ignoring the upstream pressure that builds when the consumer cannot keep up.

I chose not to ask the follow-up about flow control. The signal was clear when they treated the queue as a buffer instead of a pressure valve.

This is usually where the discussion stops being about throughput and starts revealing how someone reasons about systemic instability

I tend to pause when this answer sounds complete.

The dashboard was lying.

Most candidates describe the Outbox pattern or transactional listeners as the final solution for dual writes. They explain how the JVM-based transaction manager ensures the event is stored in the primary database before the message broker receives it.

I almost missed it.

I let them keep talking while waiting for a mention of the repair strategy. Strong resumes usually stop here, assuming the message broker will eventually succeed.

It sounds correct until you've lived it. I almost interrupted when the candidate started discussing retries, but I chose to stay silent to see if they addressed the ownership of state.

At ten times our current volume, we couldn't tell which side was wrong anymore. If the secondary index drifts due to a logic bug or a dropped event, the system lacks a source of truth for the reconciliation process.

I chose not to ask about the reconciliation job. The signal was clear when they assumed the primary database state would always be perfectly mirrored by the listener without a checksum or a periodic audit.

This is usually where the discussion stops being about dual writes and starts revealing how someone reasons about eventual consistency repair.

Some lessons don’t resolve.
